summary.text: Cecelia Espenoza is a Democratic member of the Colorado House of Representatives from District 4 who took office on January 8, 2025, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Her career experience includes work as an attorney, judge and professor.

paragraphs.text: Cecelia Espenoza was born in Murray, Utah, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Utah in 1979 and a law degree from the University of Utah S.J. Quinney College of Law in 1982.

Her career experience includes working as an attorney, judge and professor, and Ballotpedia lists her affiliations as the Round Table of Former Immigration Judges, Denver Cafecito and the University of Utah alumni board.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she said her parents were migrant farmworkers from Colorado who settled in Utah, and that she was the first in her family to graduate college, the first tenure-track Latina to teach law in Colorado at the University of Denver, and the first Mexican-American appellate judge on the highest immigration court in the country.
Espenoza advanced from the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary without opposition and is on the general election ballot with Republican Ellwood Ervin and Bill Hare of the Forward Party.

For 2025 and 2026 she was assigned to the House Judiciary Committee, the State, Civic, Military, and Veterans Affairs Committee, the Colorado Commission on Uniform State Laws and the Statutory Revision Committee, which she chaired.
In the survey, she listed housing and affordability, criminal and judicial justice reform, and transparency and privacy protection as her campaign priorities.
